text: This baby shop stock jumped thirteen percent in one day, on about seventy five times its usual volume. Yet it still trades at less than half its IPO price. Why?
Meet FirstCry, run by Brainbees Solutions from Pune. Founded in twenty ten, listed in twenty twenty four.

It sells almost everything for babies and kids. Diapers, clothes, toys and strollers. About two million products from over seven thousand eight hundred brands, online and in nearly twelve hundred stores.
But the smartest part of the business is hiding on the label.
Its own brands, like BabyHug, CuteWalk and Pine Kids. When FirstCry sells its own brand, it doesn't have to share the margin with an outside company.
It runs four businesses. The India business, the biggest one. Online shopping in the UAE and Saudi Arabia. GlobalBees, a group of online brands. And Intellitots preschools.

Now, the profit. In the September quarter, revenue grew fourteen percent to two thousand three hundred ninety six crore rupees. And the loss shrank seventy five percent, to just twelve point six crore.

That's what excited the market. The India business already made a profit last year. But the company as a whole is still in a small loss, and the share is far below its IPO price of four hundred sixty five rupees.
Would you buy the baby products, or the company that sells them? Tell me in the comments, and follow money in cloud. Education only, not a buy or sell call.
